analysis.title: GS Asia China Consumer and Healthcare, Trading desk color (Khong, 12 Nov 2026)
key_insights: US equities rallied on 11 Nov. The S&P closed +131bps at 7,619, NDX rose about 225bps and is back above its 200-day moving average, and the VIX is at a 17 handle. The desk attributes the move to cleaner positioning, falling index vol and election narratives being digested, not to overnight earnings. The bond market was closed for Veterans Day.
NDX is back above its pre-election level and SOX is approaching its own 200-day moving average.

Retail participation was strong. The GS Retail Favorite basket rose +495bps, its third best day in three years. Floor activity was 5 out of 10, with asset managers and hedge funds net buyers on a re-risk across semis.

The trading desk sees relatively little consensus in the market for the first time in a while. Debate centres on where the AI/semis cycle stands, what is priced in, and whether this is a bear market bounce or a bull market forming (year-end rally). Software dispersion has picked up, including within cyber and data infrastructure. Internet is squeezy and hard to trade. Hyperscaler sentiment is the one possible exception. The desk reads the 'blank slate' on positioning as a healthy backdrop into 2027.
Taiwan and Korea desks reported limit-order bids in TSMC and Samsung on 11 Nov.

Hong Kong high-touch flows: total notional was in line with the 4-week average while the index underperformed the region. Healthcare saw profit-taking and a yield headwind but decent inflows (Innovent, WuXi AppTec, WuXi Bio, new hedge fund bids in JD Health). China banks, mainly CCB, drew standout limit-order inflows on a defensive/high-dividend theme.

HK tech flows were mixed: selling soft platforms such as BABA, buying hardware (Lenovo, Montage, Innolight, plus A-share 300308). Consumer was two-way: selling travel and tourism (Sands, Samsonite), buying Tsingtao. In industrials, clients switched CATL A shares into H shares and added outright CATL H.
Southbound inflows of +$580m were the highest day since the mid-term elections, but are still -$2.3bn on net outflows since 4 November.

China Consumer 3Q26 wrap-up: muted demand, cost inflation and operating deleverage drove broad-based earnings misses. Household cash flow is pressured by a still-elevated saving rate. 2027 cost resets and selective pass-through are the key debates, and growth deceleration is a rising worry for structural winners.

China consumer preferences: continue to prefer restaurants, F&B value retailers, dairy, condiments, snacks and leading white goods. Turn neutral on projectors and on apparel and footwear OEMs (rising overseas contribution, easier 2H26 base). Least preferred: furniture, discretionary small kitchen appliances, non-super-premium spirits, sports retailers and pet food.

China Banks: Bloomberg reported that authorities are assessing a 25% income tax on interest from central and local government bonds. The report does not say whether or when the tax treatment will change, or whether existing holdings would be included. GS models the earnings impact under different scope assumptions and the OCI valuation impact if government-bond yields reprice higher.

China CRO/CDMO 3Q26: robust order momentum and faster capacity expansion improve 2027 visibility despite market volatility. WuXi AppTec new orders accelerated to roughly 60% YoY in 9M26, and it raised FY26 continuing-operations revenue growth guidance to 40%-42% from 35%-39%. The recovery is broadening into early-stage activity, with AI-based drug discovery a new demand driver. Geopolitical risk eased after WuXi AppTec's removal from the Pentagon's Section 1260H list. GS prefers WuXi AppTec, Pharmaron and GenScript.

China Healthcare Corp Day (70+ management teams): the investor debate has moved from re-entry to positioning for 2027. CDMO remains the preferred subsector. Biotech go-global depends on clinical and regulatory validation of China-originated assets. Pharma recovery is divergent, with new launches offsetting legacy weakness.

GS is incrementally more positive on WuXi AppTec, Pharmaron and Mindray (commercial order validation, channel destocking ending) and more cautious on Topchoice Medical, CMS and CR Pharm (volume and pricing pressure).

Rating changes listed: Suja Life (SUJA) downgraded to Neutral after pressured Q3 and lowered FY26 guidance, PGHN and TKO cut to Sell, Pluxee upgraded to Neutral, Kurita Water downgraded to Neutral from Buy.
Recent GS macro headlines listed include 'US Daily: Adding a Third Hike in March' and an EM MarketStrats note saying two consecutive hot CPI prints show the Fed is behind the curve.

WuXi AppTec raised FY26 continuing-operations revenue growth guidance to 40%-42% from 35%-39%. 9M26 new orders accelerated to roughly 60% YoY. 3Q26 CRO/CDMO earnings were broadly solid despite FX headwinds.

Suja Life (SUJA) Q3 results were pressured and FY26 guidance was lowered. GS expects FY27 growth below the algorithm.

tension_points.bull_case: A bull market may be forming with a possible year-end rally. NDX is back above its pre-election level, SOX is near its 200-day moving average, positioning is cleaner, vol has reset to a 17 handle, and sentiment on hyperscalers is positive.
tension_points.bear_case: The move could be a bear market bounce. There is open debate about where the AI/semis cycle stands and what is priced in, and dispersion in software has picked up.
